title: 半途而废
subtitle: 织到一半的布
origin: 成语见《礼记·中庸》；本书借鉴《后汉书·列女传》乐羊子妻劝学故事，作儿童化改编。
adaptationNote: 保留求学归来与织布比喻，将剪断织物改为提问，并补充算数课堂、休息、分步学习、同伴求助与返家团聚情节；这些细节属于改编。

moral.zh: 遇到困难可以休息、求助和调整方法，再继续完成自己认定的事情。
moral.en: When something is difficult, we can rest, ask for help, and try another way before carrying on toward our chosen goal.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻事情还没有做完，就中途停止，不再继续。
idiomMeaning.en: To stop halfway through a task and abandon it before it is finished.

everydayExample.zh: 拼图还差一点，我们歇一会儿再拼，别半途而废。
everydayExample.en: We have only a little of the puzzle left. Let's rest and then finish, rather than give up halfway.

visualAnchor: Ancient Chinese household and small village school. Yue Yangzi is a gentle 26-year-old man, oval face, dark hair in a simple topknot, moss-green cross-collar robe, navy sash, brown cloth shoes. His wife is a thoughtful 26-year-old woman with a round face, dark low bun, dusty-rose cross-collar robe, cream sash, beige cloth shoes. Their teacher is an elderly man with a short gray beard, gray cross-collar robe and dark-blue belt. Fixed props: plain wooden loom, cream half-woven cloth, bamboo writing slips, smooth wooden counting rods, small brown cloth travel bundle. Wife and husband appear as equal adult partners.

pages.zh: 傍晚，乐羊子坐在窗边，看妻子把一根根线织进布里。
pages.en: At dusk, Yue Yangzi sat by the window, watching his wife weave threads into cloth.
pages.prompt: Husband sits beside the window watching his wife at the wooden loom; cream cloth is only partly woven; quiet warm evening.

pages.zh: “我想跟老师学读书、学算数。”他望着远处的学堂说。
pages.en: “I want to learn to read and work with numbers,” he said, looking toward the school.
pages.prompt: Husband and wife pause by the open cottage doorway; husband gestures toward a small distant school; no departure yet.

pages.zh: 妻子给他收好行囊：“遇到不懂的，就慢慢问、慢慢学。”
pages.en: His wife packed his bundle. “When you don't understand, take your time and ask.”
pages.prompt: Wife packs the brown cloth bundle on a low table while husband listens; wooden loom in the background.

pages.zh: 第二天清晨，乐羊子背起行囊，沿着小路去求学。
pages.en: The next morning, Yue Yangzi carried his bundle down the path to study.
pages.prompt: Husband alone walking away along the village path at sunrise with the fixed brown bundle; hopeful wide scene.

pages.zh: 学堂里，老师领他读竹简，还用竹筹教他算数。
pages.en: At school, the teacher helped him read bamboo slips and count with wooden rods.
pages.prompt: Teacher and husband at a low school desk with bamboo slips and wooden counting rods; first lesson, no readable writing.

pages.zh: 有的题要想好久。乐羊子算了又算，还是弄不明白。
pages.en: Some problems took a long time. Yue Yangzi tried again and again but still felt puzzled.
pages.prompt: Husband alone looking thoughtfully at uneven groups of counting rods on the desk; confusion without shame.

pages.zh: 日子一天天过去，他越来越想家，没学完的内容却还有许多。
pages.en: As the days passed, he missed home more and more, with much still left to learn.
pages.prompt: Husband sits by the school window holding a partly used bundle of bamboo slips and looking toward the distant home path.

pages.zh: 一天，他收起竹简，回到了家。妻子高兴地迎了出来。
pages.en: One day, he packed his bamboo slips and returned home. His wife came out happily to welcome him.
pages.prompt: Wife greets husband at the cottage doorway in daylight; his bundle rests on one shoulder; welcoming reunion.

pages.zh: 吃过饭，妻子问：“最近学到了什么？还有哪里让你犯难？”
pages.en: After their meal, his wife asked, “What have you learned? What is still difficult?”
pages.prompt: Husband and wife sit at a low table after a meal; wife listens kindly; closed bamboo slips beside husband.

pages.zh: 乐羊子低声说：“还有好多没学会。我怕自己怎么学也学不好。”
pages.en: “There is so much I don't know,” Yue Yangzi said softly. “I'm afraid I won't be able to learn it.”
pages.prompt: Husband expresses uncertainty with relaxed lowered hands; wife listens at eye level; gentle close domestic scene.

pages.zh: 妻子带他来到织机旁。米白的布已经织出一大段，后面还连着细线。
pages.en: His wife led him to the loom. A long piece of cream cloth was woven, with fine threads still stretching beyond it.
pages.prompt: Both adults beside the loom; clearly show completed cream fabric in front and unwoven warp threads behind.

pages.zh: “最开始，这里也只有几根线。”她轻轻摸着已经织好的地方。
pages.en: “At first, there were only a few threads here,” she said, touching the woven cloth.
pages.prompt: Wife touches the finished section of cream fabric while husband studies the separate threads; focus on tactile loom details.

pages.zh: “有时织错了，我就退回一点，重新织。慢慢地，布才长起来。”
pages.en: “Sometimes I make a mistake and go back a little. I weave it again, and the cloth slowly grows.”
pages.prompt: Wife carefully corrects a small loose thread with the wooden shuttle; husband watches; no damaged or cut cloth.

pages.zh: 她指着没织完的地方：“要是在这里停下，就做不成原来想要的那匹布了。”
pages.en: She pointed to the unfinished section. “If I stop here, I won't have the whole cloth I wanted.”
pages.prompt: Wife points to the unfinished section, contrasting woven cloth and untouched warp; husband looks thoughtfully; no scissors or cutting.

pages.zh: 乐羊子望着细线想：读书也要一点点接着学，才能把不懂的连起来。
pages.en: Looking at the threads, Yue Yangzi thought: learning, too, happens a little at a time, joining what we know.
pages.prompt: Husband thoughtfully holds several bamboo slips beside the loom while wife stands nearby; no thought bubbles or written symbols.

pages.zh: “我会想你，也会累。”他说。妻子点头：“歇一歇，再想想怎样继续。”
pages.en: “I'll miss you, and I'll get tired,” he said. His wife nodded. “Rest, then think about how to carry on.”
pages.prompt: Husband and wife share a calm conversation on a courtyard bench; bundle set aside; restful evening, no pressure.

pages.zh: 休息过后，他把难题分成小步，又收好行囊，回学堂向老师请教。
pages.en: After resting, he divided the difficult work into smaller steps, packed his bundle, and returned to ask his teacher.
pages.prompt: Husband stands at the school doorway with his bundle; teacher welcomes him; bamboo slips tied into small separate bundles.

pages.zh: 这回，他先学懂一小段，再往下学。卡住了，就问老师，也和同伴一起试。
pages.en: This time, he learned one small part before moving on. When he got stuck, he asked his teacher and tried with a classmate.
pages.prompt: Husband and teacher work through one small group of counting rods; one adult classmate in a plain cream robe observes; no crowded school.

pages.zh: 一段时间后，乐羊子完成了这次要学的内容，带着整理好的竹简回家。
pages.en: After some time, Yue Yangzi finished the lessons he had set out to learn and brought his organized bamboo slips home.
pages.prompt: Husband walks toward his cottage carrying a neatly tied completed bundle of bamboo slips; warm late-afternoon path.

pages.zh: 妻子展开织好的布，乐羊子讲起学会的办法。屋里，线和学问都连成了新的模样。
pages.en: His wife unfolded her finished cloth, and Yue Yangzi shared what he had learned. Both their efforts had become something new.
pages.prompt: Husband and wife together at a low table; full cream cloth drapes from the completed loom, neatly tied bamboo slips open beside them; warm mutual pride.

title: 一诺千金
subtitle: 答应好的木偶戏
origin: 依据成语含义创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 答应之前认真考虑，答应之后努力做到；遇到困难，及时沟通并寻找办法。
moral.en: Think before making a promise, work to keep it, and speak up promptly when difficulties arise.

idiomMeaning.zh: 形容说话算数，承诺很有分量，值得信任。
idiomMeaning.en: A promise worth a thousand pieces of gold: being trustworthy and keeping one's word.

everydayExample.zh: 他说星期六来帮忙，果然来了，真是一诺千金。
everydayExample.en: He said he would help on Saturday, and he did. He really keeps his word.

visualAnchor: Cozy woodland village. Young russet Fox with cream muzzle and tail tip, teal waistcoat; young brown Hedgehog with soft rounded spines, yellow shirt; young white Rabbit with peach dress; adult brown Bear carpenter with sage-green work apron. Fixed props: small tabletop puppet booth with blue cloth curtain, green FROG hand puppet and yellow DUCK hand puppet, wooden support bars, plain invitation card with a painted hedgehog face and flower border, no lettering. Puppets are small cloth props, not extra live animals.

pages.zh: 小刺猬的生日快到了。他捧着一张自己画的邀请卡，来找小狐狸。
pages.en: Hedgehog's birthday was coming. He brought Fox an invitation card he had painted himself.
pages.prompt: Hedgehog offers the illustrated invitation card to Fox at Fox's cottage doorway; cheerful morning.

pages.zh: “星期六下午，我给你演木偶戏！”小狐狸想了想，认真答应了。
pages.en: “I'll put on a puppet show for you on Saturday afternoon!” Fox thought it over and made his promise.
pages.prompt: Fox and Hedgehog agree on the puppet show beside the low table; closed blue-curtain booth visible behind Fox.

pages.zh: 他找出一只青蛙手偶、一只小鸭手偶，把小舞台擦得干干净净。
pages.en: He found a frog puppet and a duck puppet and wiped his little stage clean.
pages.prompt: Fox alone cleaning the fixed tabletop booth; exactly two cloth hand puppets lie on the table, green frog and yellow duck.

pages.zh: 青蛙跳过小河，小鸭摇摇摆摆。小狐狸一边排练，一边笑。
pages.en: The frog hopped over a stream, and the duck waddled along. Fox laughed as he rehearsed.
pages.prompt: Fox rehearses behind the booth, holding the two fixed hand puppets above the edge; playful single performance scene, no audience.

pages.zh: 星期四，小兔跑来邀请他：“周末集市开啦，星期六一起去吧！”
pages.en: On Thursday, Rabbit invited him. “The weekend market is opening! Let's go on Saturday!”
pages.prompt: Rabbit invites Fox outside his cottage with a plain basket in hand; no market scene or readable signs.

pages.zh: 小狐狸听得耳朵竖起来：甜甜的点心、会转的小风车，他都想看。
pages.en: Fox's ears perked up. He wanted to see the sweet treats and the spinning pinwheels.
pages.prompt: Fox looks excited while Rabbit gestures enthusiastically; small plain paper pinwheel in Rabbit's basket; no fantasy collage.

pages.zh: “下午最热闹！”小兔说。小狐狸看看邀请卡，心里忽然打了个结。
pages.en: “The afternoon is the busiest!” said Rabbit. Fox looked at the invitation and suddenly felt torn.
pages.prompt: Fox studies Hedgehog's invitation on the doorstep while Rabbit stands beside him; booth visible inside; conflicting feelings.

pages.zh: 他差点想说自己忘了，又把话咽了回去。小刺猬一定在等这场戏。
pages.en: He almost said he had forgotten, then stopped himself. Hedgehog would be waiting for the show.
pages.prompt: Fox alone at the low table, looking between the painted invitation and the two cloth puppets; thoughtful hesitation.

pages.zh: 邀请卡上，小刺猬画了三个笑脸。小狐狸轻轻摸了摸那个属于自己的。
pages.en: Hedgehog had painted three smiling faces on the card. Fox gently touched the one that looked like him.
pages.prompt: Close view of Fox holding the invitation with simple hedgehog, fox and rabbit portrait icons; no letters or numbers.

pages.zh: 他去找小兔：“我已经答应小刺猬了，星期六下午要留给木偶戏。”
pages.en: He went to Rabbit. “I already promised Hedgehog. Saturday afternoon is for the puppet show.”
pages.prompt: Fox speaks openly with Rabbit on a woodland path; invitation in his paw; calm sincere expressions.

pages.zh: 小兔点点头：“集市星期天也开。那我们星期天一起去！”
pages.en: Rabbit nodded. “The market is open on Sunday too. We can go then!”
pages.prompt: Rabbit and Fox smile at a new plan beside the path; Rabbit holds the same small basket; no written calendar.

pages.zh: 小狐狸高高兴兴回家。可一碰舞台，右边的木支架竟晃了起来。
pages.en: Fox returned home happily. But when he touched the stage, its right wooden support wobbled.
pages.prompt: Fox gently tests the right support of the small puppet booth; visibly loose joint, intact blue curtain; puppets on table.

pages.zh: 他扶住支架，心里发慌：“要是演到一半倒了，可怎么办？”
pages.en: He steadied the support and worried. “What if it falls during the show?”
pages.prompt: Fox holds the loose booth support still; worried but safe; tabletop stage remains upright, no collapse.

pages.zh: 这次，他没有悄悄躲开，而是告诉小刺猬：“舞台坏了，我正在想办法。”
pages.en: This time he didn't hide. He told Hedgehog, “The stage needs fixing. I'm working on a way to do it.”
pages.prompt: Fox explains the problem to Hedgehog beside the booth; loose support clearly visible; Hedgehog listens kindly.

pages.zh: “我们一起看看吧。”小刺猬说。小兔也请来了会修木头的熊伯伯。
pages.en: “Let's look together,” said Hedgehog. Rabbit brought Bear, who knew how to repair wooden things.
pages.prompt: Fox, Hedgehog, Rabbit and adult Bear carpenter gather around the small booth, looking at its support; no repairs completed yet.

pages.zh: 熊伯伯找到松动的地方，装上一块支撑木。小伙伴们帮忙扶稳舞台。
pages.en: Bear found the loose joint and fitted a wooden brace. The friends helped keep the stage steady.
pages.prompt: Adult Bear fits a short diagonal wooden brace to the booth while Fox and Hedgehog hold its edges; Rabbit holds the blue curtain aside; no unsafe child tools.

pages.zh: 小狐狸轻轻试了试：不晃了！青蛙和小鸭又能在蓝幕布前见面了。
pages.en: Fox tested it gently. No wobble! The frog and duck could meet in front of the blue curtain again.
pages.prompt: Fox tests the repaired stable booth, green frog and yellow duck puppets resting together at its edge; visible new wooden brace.

pages.zh: 星期五晚上，他再排练一遍，把需要的东西一件件收进小箱子。
pages.en: On Friday evening, he rehearsed once more and packed everything into a little box.
pages.prompt: Fox packs the two hand puppets into a small brown box beside the repaired booth; evening lamplight, no extra puppet characters.

pages.zh: 生日那天下午，小刺猬摆好点心，小兔在窗边挂起纸花。
pages.en: On the birthday afternoon, Hedgehog set out snacks while Rabbit hung paper flowers by the window.
pages.prompt: Hedgehog sets a low snack table, Rabbit hangs paper flowers, Fox positions the repaired booth at one side; no active show yet.

pages.zh: 蓝幕布拉开，青蛙跳出来，小鸭跟着摇摇摆摆。木偶戏准时开始了。
pages.en: The blue curtain opened. Out hopped the frog, followed by the waddling duck. The show began on time.
pages.prompt: Fox operates both small hand puppets behind the repaired booth; Hedgehog and Rabbit sit in front enjoying the birthday show.

pages.zh: 小刺猬笑得直拍手：“这只小鸭太好玩啦！”小狐狸也开心地笑了。
pages.en: Hedgehog clapped and laughed. “That duck is so funny!” Fox beamed too.
pages.prompt: Hedgehog and Rabbit applaud the two cloth puppets above the blue curtain; Fox visible behind the booth, joyful.

pages.zh: 第二天逛集市时，小狐狸心里暖暖的。守住一个承诺，也守住了朋友的信任。
pages.en: At the market the next day, Fox felt warm inside. By keeping his promise, he had kept his friend's trust.
pages.prompt: Fox and Rabbit walk through a gentle woodland Sunday market with simple stalls and paper pinwheels; no readable signs; peaceful ending.

title: 雪中送炭
subtitle: 雪天送来的热汤
origin: 依据成语含义创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 在别人困难的时候，先听听他需要什么，再送上合适的帮助。
moral.en: When someone is having a hard time, first listen to what they need, then offer help that fits.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻在别人急需帮助时，给予及时而切实的支持。
idiomMeaning.en: Sending charcoal in snowy weather: offering timely, practical support when someone needs it most.

everydayExample.zh: 我正发愁怎么搬这些箱子，你就来帮忙了，真是雪中送炭！
everydayExample.en: I was worrying about moving these boxes, and you came to help just when I needed it!

visualAnchor: Snowy woodland village with a small new timber cottage. Young gray Badger with distinct dark cheek stripes, sky-blue waistcoat; adult gray Badger mother with matching natural face markings, rust-red apron; young white Rabbit in a peach coat and teal scarf; adult white Rabbit mother in an olive coat and cream scarf; adult brown Bear neighbor in a green work apron. Fixed props: rabbit's small paper flowers in a plain cream envelope, covered brown soup pot, dry food basket, thick mustard-yellow blanket, wood-and-clay pantry beneath a visibly loose roof seam. Adults handle hot soup and household repairs.

pages.zh: 小獾和妈妈刚搬到森林边。新家的窗外，有一棵高高的松树。
pages.en: Badger and his mother had just moved to the edge of the forest. A tall pine stood outside their new window.
pages.prompt: Badger and Badger mother at the doorway of their small timber cottage; tall pine nearby, moving baskets still on porch; cold clear weather.

pages.zh: 他们把干粮放进储藏室，又把厚被子铺到床上，准备迎接冬天。
pages.en: They put dry food in the pantry and spread a thick quilt on the bed, getting ready for winter.
pages.prompt: Badger and mother place covered food baskets on a pantry shelf; thick neutral cream quilt visible through an adjacent doorway; no snow leak yet.

pages.zh: 没过几天，大雪来了。松枝低低垂着，小路也披上白白的一层。
pages.en: A few days later, snow arrived. Pine branches bowed low, and a white layer covered the path.
pages.prompt: Exterior of the fixed cottage in falling snow, bowed pine branches and white path; Badger watches through the window.

pages.zh: 夜里，储藏室的屋顶漏了水。滴答，滴答，水落在粮袋旁边。
pages.en: That night, water leaked through the pantry roof. Drip, drip—it fell beside the food bags.
pages.prompt: Badger mother notices drips at one loose pantry roof seam by lamplight; small puddle near food baskets; gentle ordinary leak.

pages.zh: 獾妈妈连忙把东西搬开，可几袋干粮已经湿了，角落里的被子也潮了。
pages.en: Badger's mother moved things out of the way, but some food bags were wet, and a spare quilt in the corner was damp.
pages.prompt: Badger mother lifts damp food bags to a dry shelf; Badger holds an empty basket; wet spare cream quilt folded on a low stool.

pages.zh: 小獾裹着衣服，望着空了许多的架子，心里有些发愁。
pages.en: Badger wrapped his coat around himself and worried at the nearly empty shelves.
pages.prompt: Badger alone gazes at the pantry shelf with only a small dry food bundle remaining; cool morning, no frightening distress.

pages.zh: 第二天，小兔做好一束纸花，想送去庆祝小獾的新家。
pages.en: The next day, Rabbit made a bunch of paper flowers to celebrate Badger's new home.
pages.prompt: Rabbit at her home table arranging paper flowers beside the cream envelope; cheerful preparation.

pages.zh: 来到门口，她看见接水的盆和湿粮袋，连忙问：“你们还好吗？”
pages.en: At the door, she saw a basin catching drips and wet food bags. “Are you all right?” she asked.
pages.prompt: Rabbit in peach coat stands at Badger's doorway, holding the envelope; Badger and mother inside beside damp food bags and drip basin.

pages.zh: 小獾说：“我们有点冷，今天能吃的东西也不多了。”
pages.en: “We're a little cold,” said Badger. “And we don't have much food for today.”
pages.prompt: Badger explains at the doorway to Rabbit; mother sorts dry food in background; respectful conversation, no paper flowers presented yet.

pages.zh: 小兔把纸花收好：“我先回去问妈妈，看看能带些什么来。”
pages.en: Rabbit tucked the paper flowers away. “I'll ask my mother what we can bring.”
pages.prompt: Rabbit carefully closes the cream envelope while speaking to Badger; snow outside, calm practical decision.

pages.zh: 兔妈妈听完，问清小獾家的需要，找出一条干燥的厚毯子。
pages.en: Rabbit's mother listened, checked what Badger's family needed, and found a thick, dry blanket.
pages.prompt: Rabbit and her mother select the fixed mustard-yellow blanket from a dry cupboard; envelope on nearby table.

pages.zh: 她煮了一锅热汤。小兔把能直接吃的面包和果干装进篮子。
pages.en: She cooked a pot of hot soup. Rabbit packed bread and dried fruit into a basket.
pages.prompt: Adult Rabbit mother handles the covered brown soup pot in the kitchen; young Rabbit packs bread and dried fruit at a separate cool table.

pages.zh: 热汤盖好，毯子包好。妈妈提着汤锅，小兔抱起装干粮的篮子。
pages.en: The soup was covered and the blanket wrapped. Mother carried the pot, and Rabbit picked up the food basket.
pages.prompt: Rabbit mother securely holds covered soup pot and wrapped mustard blanket; Rabbit lifts dry food basket beside the home door.

pages.zh: 她们沿着清扫过的小路，一步一步走到小獾家。
pages.en: They followed the cleared path, step by step, to Badger's home.
pages.prompt: Rabbit mother and young Rabbit walk slowly along a cleared flat snowy path carrying the fixed supplies; daylight, no storm danger.

pages.zh: 獾妈妈接过毯子，给小獾裹在肩上。软软的暖意慢慢围住了他。
pages.en: Badger's mother took the blanket and wrapped it around him. Soft warmth settled over his shoulders.
pages.prompt: Badger mother wraps the mustard-yellow blanket around seated Badger; Rabbit and mother set supplies on the low table.

pages.zh: 四只小碗摆上桌，热汤冒着轻轻的白气。大家坐下来，慢慢喝。
pages.en: Four little bowls went on the table, with wisps of steam rising from the soup. Everyone sat and sipped slowly.
pages.prompt: Badger, Badger mother, Rabbit and Rabbit mother seated at a low table with four warm soup bowls; covered pot nearby; no burns.

pages.zh: “你们送来的，正是我们最需要的。”獾妈妈握着兔妈妈的手说。
pages.en: “You brought just what we needed,” said Badger's mother, taking Rabbit's mother's hand.
pages.prompt: The two mothers share a grateful hand clasp beside the table; children finish bread quietly, blanket stays on Badger.

pages.zh: 下午，熊伯伯来帮忙，从屋里补好漏水的地方。储藏室终于不再滴答了。
pages.en: That afternoon, Bear helped seal the leak from inside. At last, the pantry stopped dripping.
pages.prompt: Adult Bear works from a stable indoor platform sealing the low pantry roof seam; Badger mother watches from below, dry drip basin under the seam.

pages.zh: 天放晴后，小兔再来，把纸花挂在窗边。这回，小獾开心地帮她挑位置。
pages.en: When the sky cleared, Rabbit returned with the paper flowers. This time Badger happily helped choose a spot.
pages.prompt: Rabbit and Badger hang the same paper flowers at a reachable cottage window; mustard blanket neatly folded, clear winter daylight.

pages.zh: 雪还堆在屋外，屋里却暖暖的。小獾记住了那天及时送来的热汤。
pages.en: Snow still lay outside, but the room felt warm. Badger remembered the soup that had arrived just when he needed it.
pages.prompt: Warm wide cottage ending: Badger and mother at table with Rabbit and mother visiting; paper flowers at window, folded mustard blanket, snowy pine outside.

title: 取长补短
subtitle: 三位朋友的游园会海报
origin: 依据成语含义创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 发现彼此的长处，愿意学习和分享，就能一起进步。
moral.en: Notice one another's strengths, share what you know, and learn from each other.

idiomMeaning.zh: 吸取别人的长处，弥补自己的不足。
idiomMeaning.en: To learn from another person's strengths and improve one's own weaker skills.

everydayExample.zh: 你会画画，我会写字，我们可以取长补短。
everydayExample.en: You draw well and I write neatly. We can learn from each other's strengths.

visualAnchor: Sunny woodland art room and village noticeboard. Young white Rabbit in mint-green dress and yellow hair ribbon; young small olive-green Tortoise with brown shell, blue vest, round friendly face; young russet Squirrel with cream belly and plum-purple shirt. Fixed props: large cream poster paper, smaller cream invitation cards, blue paint cup, red paint cup, yellow paint cup, short brushes, plain wooden ruler. Rabbit is best at expressive drawings, Tortoise at neat writing, Squirrel at layout. Show writing actions from angles that keep actual letters out of frame; posters may show simple flower, path and animal icons with blank title bands.

pages.zh: 森林要办游园会，三位朋友都想画一张海报，邀请大家来玩。
pages.en: The forest was holding a fair. Three friends each wanted to make a poster inviting everyone.
pages.prompt: Rabbit, Tortoise and Squirrel gather at the art table with three blank cream poster sheets and paint cups.

pages.zh: 小兔抱来颜料，小乌龟摆好毛笔，小松鼠摊开一张大纸。
pages.en: Rabbit brought paints, Tortoise set out brushes, and Squirrel spread a large sheet of paper.
pages.prompt: Three friends begin separate posters at the same table, each arranging their fixed tools; all paper still mostly blank.

pages.zh: 小兔画的小动物活灵活现，可写上时间和地点后，纸上挤得快没空了。
pages.en: Rabbit's animals looked lively, but once she added the time and place, her poster was almost too crowded.
pages.prompt: Rabbit examines a poster filled with lively animal and flower pictures, very little blank space; no readable letters.

pages.zh: 小乌龟的字一行行排得整齐，却不知道用什么颜色，海报显得有些单调。
pages.en: Tortoise's writing was neat, but he wasn't sure which colors to choose. His poster looked a little plain.
pages.prompt: Tortoise at a restrained monochrome poster, brush in hand; camera from the back avoids all readable writing.

pages.zh: 小松鼠留好了每块位置，可画出的小兔像个圆球，自己也认不出来。
pages.en: Squirrel planned every space, but his rabbit drawing looked like a round ball, even to him.
pages.prompt: Squirrel looks at an orderly poster layout with a simple round ambiguous rabbit doodle; no letters or ridicule.

pages.zh: 三张海报摆在一起。小兔叹气，小乌龟皱眉，小松鼠挠了挠头。
pages.en: They set out all three posters. Rabbit sighed, Tortoise frowned, and Squirrel scratched his head.
pages.prompt: Three friends calmly inspect the three visibly different incomplete posters together; mild frustration.

pages.zh: 小乌龟先说：“小兔，你画的耳朵和眼睛，一看就知道是谁！”
pages.en: “Rabbit, your ears and eyes make it easy to tell who's who!” Tortoise said first.
pages.prompt: Tortoise points appreciatively to Rabbit's recognizable animal drawing; Rabbit listens, Squirrel nearby.

pages.zh: 小兔也发现：“小松鼠，你给每一部分留的位置，真舒服呀。”
pages.en: Rabbit noticed too. “Squirrel, you've left just the right amount of space for each part.”
pages.prompt: Rabbit gestures toward Squirrel's balanced layout; Squirrel smiles; blank title and content spaces remain visible.

pages.zh: 小松鼠凑近小乌龟的纸：“你的字这么整齐，可以教教我们吗？”
pages.en: Squirrel leaned toward Tortoise's paper. “Your writing is so neat. Will you teach us?”
pages.prompt: Squirrel asks Tortoise beside his poster; brush grip shown without any actual lettering; Rabbit watches.

pages.zh: 小乌龟笑了：“可以！我也想学学，怎样把颜色搭得好看。”
pages.en: Tortoise smiled. “Yes! I'd like to learn how to choose colors that work together.”
pages.prompt: Tortoise offers the short brush while looking at Rabbit's red, yellow and blue paint cups; cheerful exchange.

pages.zh: 小兔画了两只小耳朵，让小松鼠慢慢试。小松鼠这回画得像多了。
pages.en: Rabbit drew two little ears for Squirrel to try. This time his drawing looked much more like a rabbit.
pages.prompt: Rabbit demonstrates two rounded rabbit ears on a small practice sheet; Squirrel tries beside her; simple picture icons only.

pages.zh: “不如一起做一张大海报！”三个脑袋凑到同一张空白纸前。
pages.en: “Let's make one big poster together!” Three heads leaned over a fresh sheet.
pages.prompt: All three friends lean toward one large blank cream poster sheet; earlier practice sheets neatly set aside.

pages.zh: 小松鼠先安排位置：上面留给名字，中间画游园路线，下面放小提示。
pages.en: Squirrel planned the spaces: a title at the top, a fair map in the middle, and little reminders below.
pages.prompt: Squirrel uses plain ruler to indicate three broad empty poster zones; Rabbit and Tortoise listen; no guide letters.

pages.zh: 小兔在中间画出花园、游戏摊和笑眯眯的小伙伴。
pages.en: Rabbit drew a garden, game stalls, and smiling friends in the middle.
pages.prompt: Rabbit paints a simple central fair map with flowers and small animal portrait icons; broad top and bottom spaces still blank.

pages.zh: 小乌龟慢慢写好内容，提醒大家：每一行都要给下一行留些地方。
pages.en: Tortoise added the information carefully. “Each line needs room for the next,” he reminded them.
pages.prompt: Over Tortoise's shoulder as he writes in a reserved top band; hand and paper angle conceal any letters; Rabbit and Squirrel watch spacing.

pages.zh: 三个人退后看看，又把一朵挡住路线的小花挪到了旁边。
pages.en: They stepped back to look, then moved a flower that was covering part of the route.
pages.prompt: Three friends evaluate the nearly finished poster; Rabbit moves a small paper flower decoration off the winding route icon.

pages.zh: 海报挂上木板，经过的朋友停下来，很快就找到自己想玩的地方。
pages.en: They hung the poster on the board. Passing friends stopped and quickly found the activities they liked.
pages.prompt: Rabbit, Tortoise and Squirrel beside a village noticeboard with their balanced map poster; two small distant animal visitors point to map icons.

pages.zh: “原来，我们会的东西能互相帮忙。”小松鼠望着海报，笑了起来。
pages.en: “The things we know can help each other,” Squirrel said with a smile.
pages.prompt: Squirrel shares a pleased realization with Rabbit and Tortoise beside the completed poster; friendly eye contact.

pages.zh: 回到桌前，他们各做一张小邀请卡，再试试刚学会的新办法。
pages.en: Back at the table, each made a little invitation card, trying the new skills they had learned.
pages.prompt: All three friends work independently on small cards at the art table; Rabbit leaves more space, Tortoise selects warm colors, Squirrel draws recognizable ears.

pages.zh: 小兔留出了空白，小乌龟添了颜色，小松鼠画好了耳朵。三张小卡，都比刚才更好了。
pages.en: Rabbit left room, Tortoise added color, and Squirrel drew clear ears. Each little card was better than before.
pages.prompt: Three friends proudly hold their distinct improved invitation cards with simple flower and rabbit icons; no readable words; warm art-room ending.

title: 将心比心
subtitle: 小熊也想把话说完
origin: 依据成语含义创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 试着站在别人的位置体会他的感受，也认真听他说出自己的需要。
moral.en: Imagine how someone else feels in their situation, and listen to what they need.

idiomMeaning.zh: 拿自己的感受去体会别人的处境，设身处地为别人着想。
idiomMeaning.en: To put oneself in another person's place and consider their feelings.

everydayExample.zh: 你也希望别人认真听你说话，我们将心比心，先听他说完。
everydayExample.en: You want others to listen when you speak. Let's put ourselves in his place and let him finish.

visualAnchor: Woodland friends planning a daytime camping visit in a sheltered meadow. Young honey-brown Bear with cream muzzle and sky-blue vest; young russet Squirrel with cream belly and orange shirt; young white Rabbit in a yellow dress. Fixed props: plain low round wooden planning table, blank cream planning sheet with simple landscape icons, blue paper lantern with small cream moon pictures and no flame, a single smooth pinecone used as a turn-taking token, one small green fabric tent. Warm caring expressions, no adults required for the illustrated conversational scenes.

pages.zh: 森林露营日快到了，小熊、小松鼠和小兔坐到树下，一起商量带些什么。
pages.en: The forest camping day was coming. Bear, Squirrel, and Rabbit sat beneath a tree to plan what to bring.
pages.prompt: Bear, Squirrel and Rabbit gather around the low planning table beneath a broad tree; blank planning sheet and pinecone.

pages.zh: 小熊有好多主意：带灯笼、讲故事，还要准备一张软软的垫子。
pages.en: Bear had so many ideas: a lantern, stories, and a soft mat to sit on.
pages.prompt: Bear eagerly gestures as Rabbit and Squirrel listen; simple mat and lantern picture icons on the planning sheet.

pages.zh: 小松鼠刚说：“搭帐篷的地方，我想……”小熊就兴奋地接上话。
pages.en: Squirrel began, “About where to put the tent, I think…” Bear jumped in excitedly.
pages.prompt: Squirrel starts explaining a location on the sheet, but Bear leans forward to speak; Rabbit watches.

pages.zh: “我知道！就在最高的山坡上，可以看得最远！”他越说越起劲。
pages.en: “I know! On the highest hill, where we can see the farthest!” Bear said more and more eagerly.
pages.prompt: Bear points excitedly toward a distant hill while Squirrel pauses mid-gesture; no camping set up yet.

pages.zh: 小兔想问要走多久，才说了半句，小熊又开始讲自己的灯笼。
pages.en: Rabbit started to ask how long the walk would be, but Bear began talking about his lantern before she finished.
pages.prompt: Rabbit raises a paw to ask a question, Bear keeps talking with an excited smile; Squirrel listens quietly.

pages.zh: 小松鼠抱住尾巴，慢慢不说话了。小熊以为，大家都喜欢自己的办法。
pages.en: Squirrel held her tail and fell quiet. Bear thought everyone liked his plan.
pages.prompt: Squirrel sits quietly holding her tail; Rabbit looks thoughtful; Bear smiles unaware beside the planning table.

pages.zh: 下午，小熊带来新做的蓝灯笼，上面贴着弯弯的小月亮。
pages.en: That afternoon, Bear brought his new blue lantern, decorated with little crescent moons.
pages.prompt: Bear brings the fixed blue paper lantern with cream moon pictures to the garden table; Rabbit and Squirrel nearby.

pages.zh: “这个窗洞是我自己剪的，里面还……”他小心地举起来，想给大家看。
pages.en: “I cut this little window myself, and inside…” He lifted it carefully to show his friends.
pages.prompt: Bear carefully holds the lantern at chest height, pointing to a small cutout; no flame or actual written symbols.

pages.zh: 小兔忽然想起水壶，小松鼠也说起要带的球。小熊的话被挤到了一边。
pages.en: Rabbit suddenly remembered the water bottle, and Squirrel talked about bringing a ball. Bear's words were crowded out.
pages.prompt: Rabbit and Squirrel turn toward simple bottle and ball props on the table while Bear stops explaining his lantern.

pages.zh: 小熊张了张嘴，又停住了。灯笼明明举在手里，好像谁也没有看见。
pages.en: Bear opened his mouth, then stopped. He was holding the lantern, but it felt as though no one noticed.
pages.prompt: Bear holds the lantern lower with a disappointed expression; friends remain focused on their own discussion in the background.

pages.zh: “我还没说完呢。”他轻轻说。小兔停下来，转头看着他。
pages.en: “I haven't finished yet,” he said softly. Rabbit paused and turned toward him.
pages.prompt: Bear voices his feeling calmly; Rabbit turns with attentive eye contact, Squirrel begins to listen; lantern on the table.

pages.zh: “你想让我们听完，对吗？”小兔问。小熊点头：“我准备了好久。”
pages.en: “You want us to hear the whole thing?” Rabbit asked. Bear nodded. “I worked on it for a long time.”
pages.prompt: Rabbit listens to Bear at eye level beside the blue lantern; Squirrel watches thoughtfully.

pages.zh: 小熊忽然想起上午的小松鼠：她是不是也有这样的话，没能说完呢？
pages.en: Bear suddenly remembered Squirrel that morning. Had she, too, had something she wanted to finish saying?
pages.prompt: Bear turns thoughtfully toward Squirrel, who rests a paw beside the planning sheet; no flashback montage or thought bubbles.

pages.zh: 他走过去：“上午我打断你了。你想说的搭帐篷的地方，我想听一听。”
pages.en: He went over. “I interrupted you this morning. I'd like to hear where you wanted to put the tent.”
pages.prompt: Bear sincerely invites Squirrel to speak; Rabbit sits nearby, blue lantern now placed safely at the side.

pages.zh: 小松鼠说：“树旁这片草地挡风，也离水壶和休息的地方近一些。”
pages.en: Squirrel said, “This patch by the trees is sheltered from the wind and closer to our water and resting spot.”
pages.prompt: Squirrel points toward a sheltered level meadow near trees on the planning sheet and through the open garden view; friends listen.

pages.zh: 小熊这回听到了最后。小兔也说完了自己的想法，大家才一起商量。
pages.en: This time Bear listened to the end. Rabbit shared her idea too, and then they discussed them together.
pages.prompt: Three friends take a calm attentive discussion around the planning table; no one interrupts; landscape icons without words.

pages.zh: 他们约好，拿着小松果的人先说完。小熊也终于讲完了灯笼的秘密。
pages.en: They agreed that whoever held the pinecone would finish speaking first. Bear finally shared the secret of his lantern.
pages.prompt: Bear holds the single pinecone while showing the lantern's cutout to attentive Rabbit and Squirrel; warm turn-taking scene.

pages.zh: 露营那天，蓝灯笼挂在帐篷旁。三位朋友围坐着，每个人的话都有人认真听。
pages.en: On camping day, the blue lantern hung beside the tent. The three friends sat together, with someone listening carefully to each voice.
pages.prompt: Daytime sheltered meadow with one small green tent and blue moon lantern; Bear, Squirrel and Rabbit seated on a soft mat in attentive conversation.

title: 一举两得
subtitle: 落叶变成了宝贝
origin: 依据成语含义创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 多观察、多想一想，合适的办法可以同时解决两个问题。
moral.en: Look carefully and think things through: one suitable plan can solve two problems.

idiomMeaning.zh: 做一件事情，同时得到两种好处。
idiomMeaning.en: To gain two benefits from one action or plan.

everydayExample.zh: 走路去买菜，既办了事，又活动了身体，一举两得。
everydayExample.en: Walking to buy groceries gets an errand done and gives us exercise: two benefits from one trip.

editorialNote: 落叶堆肥的腐熟跨越秋冬至入夏，不呈现落叶立即变肥料，也不把未腐熟的材料直接施入菜地。
visualAnchor: Woodland path beside a vegetable garden across autumn, winter, spring and early summer. Young honey-brown Bear in ochre vest; young white Rabbit in mint-green apron and teal cap; elderly cream Goat gardener with short gray beard, moss-green apron. Fixed props: slatted rectangular cedar compost bin with simple removable lid, small wooden leaf rake, woven leaf basket, clay watering jar, two neat garden beds. Fresh red-gold leaves must gradually become dark crumbly finished compost over many months; no instant transformation. Small low basket trolley appears on the woodland path.

pages.zh: 秋风一吹，红的、黄的落叶铺满了森林小路。小熊走一步，脚下沙沙响。
pages.en: When the autumn wind blew, red and yellow leaves covered the forest path. They rustled beneath Bear's feet.
pages.prompt: Bear walks on the leaf-covered forest path beside the two vegetable beds; red and yellow foliage, autumn light.

pages.zh: 小兔推着篮子经过，轮子卡进厚厚的叶堆里，怎么也不好往前走。
pages.en: Rabbit came by with her basket trolley. Its wheels caught in a thick pile of leaves and would not roll easily.
pages.prompt: Rabbit steadies a low basket trolley with wheels caught in thick leaves on the path; Bear notices nearby.

pages.zh: “得把路清一清。”小熊拿来小耙子，把落叶拢成一堆。
pages.en: “We need to clear the path,” said Bear, bringing a little rake and gathering the leaves.
pages.prompt: Bear gently rakes leaves into a tidy pile at the path edge; Rabbit keeps her trolley still.

pages.zh: 可望着这堆叶子，他又发愁：“这么多，要放到哪里呢？”
pages.en: But looking at the pile, he wondered, “Where can we put all these leaves?”
pages.prompt: Bear and Rabbit inspect the large gathered leaf pile beside the path; puzzled thoughtful faces.

pages.zh: 另一边，小熊的菜长得慢。山羊爷爷看过土，说可以补些堆肥，让土里多些养分。
pages.en: Meanwhile, Bear's vegetables were growing slowly. Goat checked the soil and suggested compost to add nourishment.
pages.prompt: Elderly Goat examines soil in one vegetable bed beside Bear and Rabbit; modest small plants, no fertilizer applied yet.

pages.zh: 听说小路上有落叶，山羊爷爷笑了：“我们可以把两件事连起来想。”
pages.en: Hearing about the leaves, Goat smiled. “Perhaps we can think about these two jobs together.”
pages.prompt: Goat speaks with Bear and Rabbit between the leaf pile and the vegetable beds, indicating both problems.

pages.zh: “把落叶收起来做堆肥，小路就清爽了，等腐熟后，菜地也能用上。”
pages.en: “Collect the leaves for compost. The path will be clear, and once the compost is ready, the garden can use it.”
pages.prompt: Goat shows Bear and Rabbit the empty slatted cedar compost bin beside the garden; fresh leaf pile remains outside.

pages.zh: 山羊爷爷带他们摆好堆肥箱。箱子留着缝，让里面也能透气。
pages.en: Goat helped them set up the compost bin. Gaps in its sides let air reach inside.
pages.prompt: Goat and the two young animals position the empty slatted cedar bin on bare garden soil; clearly visible air gaps.

pages.zh: 小熊把落叶装进篮子，小兔沿着小路，把剩下的叶子也扫过来。
pages.en: Bear filled the basket with leaves while Rabbit swept the rest from the path.
pages.prompt: Bear scoops leaves into the woven basket; Rabbit clears the path with a small broom; compost bin visible nearby.

pages.zh: 一篮又一篮，落叶进了箱子。小路露出原来的样子，车轮轻轻一推就过去了。
pages.en: Basket after basket went into the bin. The path was clear again, and the trolley rolled along with a gentle push.
pages.prompt: Rabbit rolls the basket trolley smoothly on the cleared path; Bear tips a final basket of red-gold leaves into the bin.

pages.zh: “第一个好处已经有啦！”小兔笑着说。小熊也想快点看到第二个。
pages.en: “There's our first benefit!” Rabbit said happily. Bear was eager to see the second one too.
pages.prompt: Rabbit and Bear smile beside the clear path and fresh-leaf-filled bin; both garden beds still unchanged.

pages.zh: 山羊爷爷提醒：“叶子要慢慢分解、腐熟，今天还不能往菜地里放。”
pages.en: Goat reminded them, “The leaves must break down slowly into finished compost. They aren't ready for the garden today.”
pages.prompt: Goat gently explains beside the open bin of still-recognizable dry leaves; Bear holds an empty small pot, no application to garden.

pages.zh: 他们把较大的叶子弄碎，再添一点水，让叶堆微微湿润。
pages.en: They broke up the larger leaves and added a little water so the pile was slightly damp.
pages.prompt: Bear and Rabbit crumble dry leaves by hand; Goat carefully adds a small amount of water with the clay jar; no soaking puddles.

pages.zh: 隔些日子，山羊爷爷带他们翻动叶堆。原来的叶子渐渐变软、变碎。
pages.en: Every so often, Goat helped them turn the pile. The leaves slowly grew softer and smaller.
pages.prompt: Goat turns the compost with a plain wooden fork while Bear and Rabbit watch; partially softened leaf fragments still clearly visible.

pages.zh: 冬天来了，箱子盖好，落叶在里面慢慢变化。小路依然干干净净。
pages.en: Winter came. With the bin covered, the leaves continued their slow changes inside. The path stayed clear.
pages.prompt: Snowy winter garden with covered cedar compost bin and clear path; Bear and Rabbit visit in their fixed outfits plus simple cream scarves.

pages.zh: 春天，小熊打开盖子，有些叶片还能认出来。他和小兔又耐心等了一阵。
pages.en: In spring, Bear opened the lid. Some leaf pieces were still recognizable, so he and Rabbit waited longer.
pages.prompt: Early spring, Bear lifts the bin lid while Rabbit peers at partly decomposed leaves; new green buds outside, compost not yet finished.

pages.zh: 等到入夏，箱子里变成深色、松松的碎屑，闻起来像林子里的泥土。
pages.en: By early summer, the bin held dark, crumbly material that smelled like forest soil.
pages.prompt: Early summer open bin full of dark crumbly compost, almost no recognizable leaves; Bear and Rabbit look with quiet curiosity.

pages.zh: 山羊爷爷检查后说：“这回腐熟了。”他们才把堆肥拌进菜地的土里。
pages.en: Goat checked it. “It's ready now.” Only then did they mix the finished compost into the garden soil.
pages.prompt: Goat confirms dark finished compost; Bear and Rabbit gently mix small amounts into bare soil sections of the two garden beds.

pages.zh: 后来，小菜一天天长起来。小熊看看清爽的小路，又看看绿油油的菜地。
pages.en: Later, the vegetables grew day by day. Bear looked from the clear path to the green garden.
pages.prompt: Later in summer, Bear and Rabbit stand beside steadily growing leafy vegetables and the same clear path; empty woven basket near bin.

pages.zh: “清了小路，还给菜地添了养分。”小熊笑了，“这些落叶，真帮了两次忙！”
pages.en: “A clear path and nourishment for our garden,” Bear said with a smile. “Those leaves helped us in two ways!”
pages.prompt: Bear, Rabbit and Goat enjoy the tidy path and healthy garden together; cedar compost bin remains at the garden edge; warm summer ending.

title: 井井有条
subtitle: 小兔的种子小抽屉
origin: 依据成语含义创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 分类清楚、安排合理、用完归位，东西好找，做事也更从容。
moral.en: Sort things clearly, put them where they are useful, and return them after use to make tasks easier.

idiomMeaning.zh: 形容安排整齐、有条理，事情或物品的秩序清楚。
idiomMeaning.en: To be well organized, with things arranged clearly and in good order.

everydayExample.zh: 你的书包整理得井井有条，一下就找到作业本了。
everydayExample.en: Your schoolbag is so well organized that you found your workbook right away.

visualAnchor: Spring rabbit cottage with sunny garden. Young white Rabbit with powder-blue pinafore and peach neckerchief; elderly white Rabbit grandmother with round glasses, lavender cardigan and cream skirt. Fixed props: low wooden seed cabinet with six small drawers, dry cream paper seed packets with carrot, pea and flower pictures only, small green watering can, wooden hand rake, wicker tool basket, one large brown mixed storage box. All seeds stay dry in their packets until sowing; labels use pictures and no text.

pages.zh: 春天到了，小兔想在窗前种胡萝卜、豌豆，再种一圈漂亮的花。
pages.en: Spring had arrived. Rabbit wanted carrots, peas, and a ring of bright flowers outside her window.
pages.prompt: Rabbit looks across the sunny empty garden plots from her cottage window, holding three illustrated seed packets.

pages.zh: 她打开大箱子，里面有种子、小耙子、线绳，还有去年留下的小标签。
pages.en: She opened a big box filled with seeds, a little rake, string, and last year's labels.
pages.prompt: Rabbit opens the large mixed storage box with seed packets, wooden rake, string and picture tags jumbled together.

pages.zh: 胡萝卜种子在哪里？她翻出三张空纸，又碰倒了小水壶。
pages.en: Where were the carrot seeds? She found three blank sheets and knocked over the little watering can.
pages.prompt: Rabbit searches the cluttered box; empty green watering can tips harmlessly beside blank paper; no wet seed packets.

pages.zh: 好不容易找出一袋，她却分不清：这是菜种子，还是花种子？
pages.en: At last she found a packet, but she couldn't tell: vegetables or flowers?
pages.prompt: Rabbit examines one plain unidentified seed packet with a puzzled expression, mixed box open beside her.

pages.zh: 兔奶奶来帮忙：“先别急着下种，我们把东西认清、放好吧。”
pages.en: Grandmother came to help. “Before planting, let's identify everything and find good places for it.”
pages.prompt: Grandmother kneels beside Rabbit and the mixed box, gently suggesting a plan; low seed cabinet visible nearby.

pages.zh: 她们在桌上铺块干净的布，把箱子里的东西一件件摆出来。
pages.en: They spread a clean cloth on the table and laid out everything from the box, one piece at a time.
pages.prompt: Rabbit and grandmother carefully lay seed packets, rake, string and blank tags on a clean cloth, keeping categories apart.

pages.zh: 种子放一边，工具放一边。空纸和旧绳，也各自找到了位置。
pages.en: Seeds went on one side, tools on the other. Blank paper and old string had their own places too.
pages.prompt: Overhead view of neatly separated seeds, tools, paper and string on the table; Rabbit and grandmother arrange the last item.

pages.zh: 兔奶奶帮她认出种子。小兔在小袋上，画了胡萝卜、豌豆和小花。
pages.en: Grandmother helped identify the seeds. Rabbit drew carrots, peas, and flowers on the packets.
pages.prompt: Grandmother points out three kinds of seeds while Rabbit draws matching simple vegetable and flower icons on dry cream packets.

pages.zh: “看小图画，就知道里面是什么啦！”小兔把同一种种子放到一起。
pages.en: “The little pictures show what's inside!” Rabbit grouped packets of the same kind.
pages.prompt: Rabbit groups carrot packets, pea packets and flower packets into three distinct small piles; grandmother smiles nearby.

pages.zh: 她给小抽屉也贴上对应的图画，再把种子袋轻轻放进去。
pages.en: She put matching pictures on the drawers, then tucked the seed packets inside.
pages.prompt: Rabbit puts carrot packets into the carrot-icon drawer of the six-drawer low cabinet; pea and flower icons on other drawers.

pages.zh: 小耙子和线绳放进工具篮。水壶放在旁边，拿起来不会再碰倒东西。
pages.en: The rake and string went into the tool basket. The watering can stood beside it, easy to pick up.
pages.prompt: Rabbit sets rake and string in the wicker tool basket; green watering can upright beside it, clear space around both.

pages.zh: 小兔关上抽屉，又试着找一次。胡萝卜种子，一下就找到了！
pages.en: Rabbit closed the drawers and tried again. She found the carrot seeds right away!
pages.prompt: Rabbit opens the carrot-icon drawer confidently, lifting the matching dry seed packet; grandmother observes.

pages.zh: 第二天，她带上选好的种子和工具，来到窗前的小菜地。
pages.en: The next day, she carried her chosen seeds and tools to the little garden outside the window.
pages.prompt: Rabbit arrives at the garden bed with wicker tool basket, green watering can and carrot and pea seed packets.

pages.zh: 兔奶奶陪她松土、下种。小兔终于有时间，仔细看看每粒种子落在哪里。
pages.en: Grandmother helped her loosen the soil and sow. Rabbit finally had time to notice where each seed landed.
pages.prompt: Rabbit and grandmother sow seeds carefully in prepared soil; open seed packet kept on a dry board beside the bed.

pages.zh: 用完后，她把工具擦好，剩下的种子装回干燥的小袋，再放回原来的地方。
pages.en: Afterward, she wiped the tools, returned unused seeds to dry packets, and put everything back where it belonged.
pages.prompt: Rabbit wipes the wooden rake at a dry table and seals remaining seed packets before returning them to marked drawers.

pages.zh: 过了几天，小兔发现工具篮放得太远。她把它挪到门边，出门就能拿到。
pages.en: A few days later, Rabbit noticed the tool basket was too far away. She moved it beside the door for easy access.
pages.prompt: Rabbit moves only the light wicker tool basket to a low spot beside the cottage door; seed cabinet remains in a dry indoor place.

pages.zh: “整理好，还可以再改一改。”兔奶奶说，“适合自己用，就更方便。”
pages.en: “You can improve the arrangement as you go,” Grandmother said. “It works best when it suits you.”
pages.prompt: Grandmother and Rabbit consider the new basket position by the doorway; calm flexible organizing conversation.

pages.zh: 第一片小叶子钻出土时，小兔蹲下来笑了。小抽屉整整齐齐，花园也有了新的开始。
pages.en: When the first little leaf rose from the soil, Rabbit crouched and smiled. Her drawers were in order, and her garden had begun.
pages.prompt: Rabbit and grandmother admire a tiny first seedling in the garden; open cottage door shows tidy low seed cabinet and tool basket.

title: 事半功倍
subtitle: 小熊搬书的新办法
origin: 依据成语含义创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 先观察、找方法，合适的工具和安排能省力，也能把事情做好。
moral.en: Look at the task first. A suitable method, helpful tools, and a clear plan can save effort and improve the result.

idiomMeaning.zh: 形容方法合适，花较少的力气，取得较好的效果。
idiomMeaning.en: To achieve better results with less effort by using an effective method.

everydayExample.zh: 先列清单再去采购，可以少跑几趟，事半功倍。
everydayExample.en: Making a shopping list first can save extra trips and help us get more done with less effort.

visualAnchor: Woodland library moving books between two adjacent ground-floor rooms along a short level corridor. Young honey-brown Bear with cream muzzle and plum-purple vest; young olive-green Tortoise with brown shell and orange waistcoat; adult gray Badger librarian with dark cheek stripes and olive cardigan. Fixed props: low four-wheel wooden trolley with a wide handle, small plain brown book boxes, shelves with leaf, paw and star picture markers, books with colored blank spines and no titles, plain wooden measuring stick. Loads remain low, stable and manageable; no tall leaning stacks.

pages.zh: 森林图书馆要换到旁边的大房间，小熊一早就来帮忙。
pages.en: The forest library was moving to the larger room next door. Bear arrived early to help.
pages.prompt: Bear arrives in the old library room with full wooden shelves; doorway to adjacent larger room visible across short level corridor.

pages.zh: 他抱起几本书，沿着走廊跑过去，放到新书架上。
pages.en: He picked up a few books, hurried along the corridor, and placed them on a new shelf.
pages.prompt: Bear carries a small manageable book pile along the level corridor toward the new room; no fall or oversized load.

pages.zh: 放好书，再回来；抱起书，再过去。小熊来来回回走了好多趟。
pages.en: Put down books, go back; pick up books, go again. Bear made trip after trip.
pages.prompt: Bear returns along the empty corridor toward the old shelves, looking slightly tired; single continuous scene, no montage.

pages.zh: 有一次，他走到新房间才发现，这几本应该放在另一边的架子上。
pages.en: Once, he reached the new room and realized the books belonged on shelves at the far side.
pages.prompt: Bear stands puzzled by a star-marked shelf holding books with leaf picture stickers; matching leaf shelf visible farther away.

pages.zh: 忙了好一会儿，小熊累得坐下来。旧书架上，还剩着好多书。
pages.en: After a while, Bear sat down, tired. There were still many books on the old shelves.
pages.prompt: Bear rests on a low stool by the still mostly full old library shelves; no injury, calm fatigue.

pages.zh: 小乌龟来了。他没有马上搬，先看看两个房间，又看看中间的走廊。
pages.en: Tortoise arrived. Before moving anything, he looked at both rooms and the corridor between them.
pages.prompt: Tortoise surveys the level corridor from the old room doorway while Bear rests; both room entrances visible.

pages.zh: 小熊有点着急：“书这么多，你怎么还在看呀？”
pages.en: Bear felt impatient. “There are so many books. Why are you still looking?”
pages.prompt: Bear questions Tortoise gently beside the old shelves; Tortoise is considering the clear route.

pages.zh: 獾馆长说：“先找到省力的办法，后面就能少走些冤枉路。”
pages.en: Badger the librarian said, “A useful plan now can save extra work later.”
pages.prompt: Adult Badger librarian joins Bear and Tortoise, pointing along the short corridor toward the new shelving.

pages.zh: 他们先把走廊边的空筐收好，留出一条宽宽的路。
pages.en: They moved the empty baskets out of the corridor, leaving a wide, clear path.
pages.prompt: Bear, Tortoise and librarian move empty light baskets into a side nook, clearing the whole level corridor.

pages.zh: 小乌龟量过门口，找到一辆能顺利通过的小推车。
pages.en: Tortoise measured the doorway and found a little trolley that would fit through.
pages.prompt: Tortoise checks doorway width with the plain measuring stick beside the low four-wheel wooden trolley; Bear watches.

pages.zh: 獾馆长拿来小箱子，按新书架的位置，把书分好，再贴上图画标记。
pages.en: The librarian brought small boxes, sorted the books by their new shelves, and added matching picture markers.
pages.prompt: Librarian sorts books into small brown boxes with leaf, paw and star picture stickers; matching new shelf markers in background.

pages.zh: 小熊想一次装很多。小乌龟说：“先装一小箱，试试重量和转弯。”
pages.en: Bear wanted to load lots at once. “Let's try one small box first,” Tortoise said, “and check the weight and turns.”
pages.prompt: Bear and Tortoise place exactly one small book box on the low trolley for a trial; other boxes remain on floor aside.

pages.zh: 小推车轻轻一推，就沿着走廊往前走，比抱在怀里轻松多了。
pages.en: With a gentle push, the trolley rolled down the corridor, much easier than carrying books in their arms.
pages.prompt: Bear pushes the trolley carrying one low box, Tortoise walks alongside; straight clear corridor.

pages.zh: 可到了门边，小熊发现箱子放偏了，拐弯时容易碰到门框。
pages.en: At the doorway, Bear noticed the box was off-center and could catch the frame when turning.
pages.prompt: Trolley pauses before the wide doorway; single box sits slightly off-center toward the side, no collision or damage.

pages.zh: 他们停下来，把箱子摆正、放低，再慢慢转过弯。这回稳稳当当。
pages.en: They stopped, centered the box low on the trolley, and turned slowly. This time it stayed steady.
pages.prompt: Bear and Tortoise turn the trolley carefully through the doorway with one centered low box; clear stable geometry.

pages.zh: 进了新房间，看见叶子标记，就把这一箱直接送到叶子书架旁。
pages.en: In the new room, they followed the leaf marker and took that box straight to the leaf shelf.
pages.prompt: Bear pushes the trolley's leaf-marked box directly beside the matching leaf shelf; no wrong-shelf detour.

pages.zh: 一箱放好，再运下一箱。小熊负责推车，小乌龟和馆长一起整理书架。
pages.en: After shelving one box, they brought the next. Bear pushed while Tortoise and the librarian arranged the books.
pages.prompt: Bear returns with a low paw-marked book box on the trolley; Tortoise and librarian shelve books beside corresponding picture markers.

pages.zh: 大家不用总是找地方、绕回头，空下来的书架越来越多。
pages.en: They no longer had to keep searching or doubling back. More and more old shelves stood empty.
pages.prompt: Old library room now has mostly empty shelves; Bear and Tortoise place the next small box on the trolley; orderly workflow.

pages.zh: 小熊擦擦额头：“原来，先想办法，真的能让后面的事轻松好多！”
pages.en: Bear wiped his forehead. “Thinking of a good way first really makes the rest easier!”
pages.prompt: Bear smiles thoughtfully at Tortoise and librarian beside the unloaded trolley in the new library.

pages.zh: 最后一本书放好，他们坐到窗边，一起打开了最喜欢的绘本。
pages.en: When the last book was in place, they sat by the window and opened their favorite picture book together.
pages.prompt: Bear, Tortoise and adult librarian read a wordless illustrated book by the bright new library window; shelves neatly filled, empty trolley parked aside.

title: 得意忘形
subtitle: 小猴的泡泡表演
origin: 依据成语含义创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 成功值得高兴，得意时也要记得分寸，留意身边的人和事情。
moral.en: Enjoy a success while staying thoughtful about what you do and the people around you.

idiomMeaning.zh: 形容因为高兴、得意，忘了应有的分寸和举止。
idiomMeaning.en: To become so pleased with oneself that one forgets to behave thoughtfully.

everydayExample.zh: 这次做得不错，可别得意忘形，后面的事情还要认真做。
everydayExample.en: You did well this time. Enjoy it, but stay thoughtful and take care with what comes next.

visualAnchor: Sunny woodland garden with a low art-and-play table. Young golden-brown Monkey with cream muzzle and teal striped vest; young white Rabbit in peach dress; young russet Fox with cream muzzle, sky-blue shirt and teal cap. Fixed props: orange circular bubble wand, broad blue bubble-solution bowl, cream drawing paper with a yellow flower picture, small white wiping cloth, colored pencils. Clear transparent soap bubbles, no balloons; spilled solution makes the original flower drawing visibly damp and wrinkled, never instantly restored.

pages.zh: 小猴在花园里学吹泡泡。橙色泡泡圈一举起来，他的眼睛就亮了。
pages.en: Monkey was learning to blow bubbles in the garden. His eyes lit up whenever he lifted the orange ring.
pages.prompt: Monkey alone at the garden table with the orange ring and blue solution bowl; excited starting practice.

pages.zh: 可他一用力吹，泡泡就破了，只有几滴水落回蓝碗里。
pages.en: But when he blew hard, the bubble burst, dropping a little liquid back into the blue bowl.
pages.prompt: Monkey blows too forcefully through the orange ring above the blue bowl; tiny harmless droplets, no large bubble.

pages.zh: 小猴慢慢试，发现轻轻吹、稳稳拿，泡泡才肯圆起来。
pages.en: He tried slowly and found that a gentle breath and a steady hand let the bubble grow round.
pages.prompt: Monkey holds the ring steadily and gently forms one small round bubble; focused face.

pages.zh: 练了好几天，他终于吹出一个大泡泡，亮晶晶地浮在阳光里。
pages.en: After several days of practice, he made a big bubble that floated, shining in the sunlight.
pages.prompt: Monkey watches a single large transparent rainbow-edged soap bubble above the orange ring; warm sunny garden.

pages.zh: 小兔放下画笔，小狐狸也拍起手：“真漂亮！”
pages.en: Rabbit put down her pencil, and Fox clapped too. “That's beautiful!”
pages.prompt: Rabbit pauses her yellow-flower drawing and Fox claps while Monkey's large bubble floats above the table; all fixed props present.

pages.zh: 小猴高兴得挺起胸膛：“我已经是森林里最会吹泡泡的啦！”
pages.en: Monkey puffed out his chest happily. “I'm the best bubble blower in the whole forest now!”
pages.prompt: Monkey proudly lifts his chin with the wand at his side; Rabbit and Fox smile nearby; no aggressive boasting pose.

pages.zh: 他又说：“下一次，我要吹一个比树还大的！”说着就蹦了起来。
pages.en: “Next I'll make one bigger than a tree!” he said, bouncing with excitement.
pages.prompt: Monkey bounces lightly beside the low table holding the orange wand; blue solution bowl remains on the table.

pages.zh: 他挥着泡泡圈转来转去，忘了蓝碗就在手边，也忘了小兔还在画画。
pages.en: He swung the bubble ring around, forgetting the bowl beside him and Rabbit's drawing on the table.
pages.prompt: Monkey swings the orange ring carelessly near the broad blue bowl; Rabbit resumes drawing, Fox watches with concern.

pages.zh: 啪嗒！他的手碰到碗沿，泡泡水洒出来，淋湿了小兔的画。
pages.en: Splash! His hand caught the rim, and bubble solution spilled onto Rabbit's picture.
pages.prompt: Monkey's hand nudges the blue bowl rim; small spill clearly wets Rabbit's cream paper with yellow flower drawing; no injury.

pages.zh: 小兔赶紧拿起画纸，纸角已经皱了：“这是我画了好久的花。”
pages.en: Rabbit quickly lifted the paper. Its corner was wrinkled. “I spent a long time drawing this flower.”
pages.prompt: Rabbit holds the visibly damp wrinkled yellow-flower picture; Monkey stops moving, Fox stands beside the table.

pages.zh: 小猴一下安静下来。大泡泡没吹出来，还把朋友的画弄湿了。
pages.en: Monkey fell quiet. He hadn't made the bigger bubble, and now his friend's picture was wet.
pages.prompt: Monkey lowers the wand with a thoughtful remorseful expression; Rabbit examines the wet paper; blue bowl upright again.

pages.zh: “对不起，我刚才只顾着得意。”他说，“我来帮忙收拾。”
pages.en: “I'm sorry. I was too busy showing off,” he said. “I'll help clean up.”
pages.prompt: Monkey sincerely apologizes to Rabbit at eye level; orange ring rests safely on the table, Fox listens.

pages.zh: 小狐狸拿来布，小猴擦干桌子，又把蓝碗放到另一边的空桌上。
pages.en: Fox brought a cloth. Monkey dried the table and moved the blue bowl to a separate empty table.
pages.prompt: Fox offers the white cloth; Monkey wipes the art table, blue bowl placed on a second low play table away from the drawing.

pages.zh: 画纸没法变回原样。小兔想了想，拿出新纸：“我再画一朵，这次要加两片叶子。”
pages.en: The paper couldn't be made as it was before. Rabbit found a fresh sheet. “I'll draw a new flower, with two leaves this time.”
pages.prompt: Rabbit sets out fresh cream paper while the original damp wrinkled flower drawing rests aside; no magical restoration.

pages.zh: 小猴帮她找好颜色，等她画完，才问：“现在，可以再试一次吗？”
pages.en: Monkey helped find the colors and waited until she finished. Then he asked, “May I try again now?”
pages.prompt: Monkey hands Rabbit yellow and green pencils as she finishes a new flower with two leaves; Fox watches kindly; bubble table separate.

pages.zh: 小兔点点头。小猴站稳，先看看四周，再轻轻蘸一圈泡泡水。
pages.en: Rabbit nodded. Monkey stood still, looked around, and gently dipped the ring into the solution.
pages.prompt: Monkey dips the orange ring calmly at the separate play table; Rabbit and Fox observe from the dry art area.

pages.zh: 这回，泡泡一个接一个飞起来。小猴很开心，手却一直稳稳的。
pages.en: This time, bubbles floated up one after another. Monkey felt happy and kept his hand steady.
pages.prompt: Monkey blows several small and medium transparent bubbles with a steady hand; blue bowl on separate table, no splash.

pages.zh: 小兔举起新画，小狐狸笑着鼓掌。小猴也笑了，把快乐轻轻放在心里。
pages.en: Rabbit held up her new picture, and Fox clapped with a smile. Monkey smiled too, enjoying his happiness quietly.
pages.prompt: Rabbit proudly holds the fresh yellow flower drawing with two green leaves; Fox claps, Monkey smiles calmly beside floating bubbles; wet original safely aside.

title: 盲人摸象
subtitle: 大象到底是什么样
origin: 传统“盲人摸象”寓言改编；人物、对话与共同了解大象的结尾作儿童化改写。
adaptationNote: 重点是把局部信息误当作整体的判断方式。人物以自然、尊重的方式描写，不以视力状况解释其性格，也不设置恢复视力的结尾。

moral.zh: 先了解更多信息，听听不同的人知道什么，再判断事情的全貌。
moral.en: Gather more information and listen to different perspectives before deciding what the whole is like.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻只凭局部了解就判断整体，不能正确认识事情的全貌。
idiomMeaning.en: To mistake knowledge of one small part for an understanding of the whole.

everydayExample.zh: 只看这一张照片还不了解事情全貌，容易盲人摸象。
everydayExample.en: One photograph doesn't show the whole situation. We could mistake a small part for the whole.

visualAnchor: Gentle traditional village elephant yard in ancient China. One calm light-gray Asian elephant with rounded natural proportions, large ears, flexible trunk, sturdy legs and thin tufted tail; no chains, no riding. Four adult friends who are blind: A-Qing, young adult man in sage-green robe and dark sash; A-Huang, adult woman in ochre-yellow robe with low black bun; A-Lan, adult man in sky-blue robe with simple topknot; A-Zi, older adult woman in lavender robe with gray low bun. Adult elephant caretaker in plain brown robe. Depict ordinary expressive faces and natural eyes without caricature, blindfolds, grotesque eye features or miraculous sight restoration. Caretaker calmly facilitates exploration; show only requested people in each scene.

pages.zh: 村里来了一头大象。它站在宽宽的院子里，耳朵轻轻扇动。
pages.en: An elephant came to the village. It stood in a wide yard, gently fanning its ears.
pages.prompt: One calm light-gray Asian elephant in a wide traditional village yard; adult caretaker in brown robe nearby; establishing scene.

pages.zh: 阿青、阿黄、阿蓝和阿紫很想认识它。他们看不见，常靠听、摸和询问了解新事物。
pages.en: A-Qing, A-Huang, A-Lan, and A-Zi wanted to know it. They were blind and often learned by listening, touching, and asking questions.
pages.prompt: The four adult friends in their fixed green, yellow, blue and lavender robes approach the caretaker at the yard entrance; respectful natural faces.

pages.zh: 照料员请他们慢慢来，陪着每个人，去摸大象不同的部位。
pages.en: The caretaker invited them to take their time and helped each explore a different part of the elephant.
pages.prompt: Caretaker explains calmly to the four friends beside the elephant, indicating where to stand; no one beneath the elephant.

pages.zh: 阿青摸到一条粗粗的腿：“原来，大象像一根结实的柱子！”
pages.en: A-Qing felt a thick leg. “So an elephant is like a sturdy pillar!”
pages.prompt: A-Qing in green robe gently feels the outside of one thick elephant leg, caretaker beside him; focus on the limited part he explores.

pages.zh: 阿黄摸到宽宽的耳朵：“不对呀，它像一把大扇子！”
pages.en: A-Huang felt a broad ear. “No, it's like a large fan!”
pages.prompt: A-Huang in ochre robe gently touches the elephant's broad lowered ear; caretaker facilitates, no other friends in close frame.

pages.zh: 阿紫摸到细细的尾巴：“我摸到的，明明像一根绳子。”
pages.en: A-Zi felt the thin tail. “What I felt was surely like a rope.”
pages.prompt: A-Zi in lavender robe gently touches the thin tail from the elephant's side with caretaker nearby; no pulling or standing directly behind.

pages.zh: 阿蓝摸到弯弯的长鼻子：“它像一根会弯的长管子，还会动呢。”
pages.en: A-Lan felt the curved trunk. “It's like a long bendy tube—and it moves.”
pages.prompt: A-Lan in blue robe touches the calm elephant's gently curved lowered trunk, caretaker close beside him; natural tactile exploration.

pages.zh: 四个人坐下来，都想告诉朋友：自己已经知道整头大象是什么样了。
pages.en: The four sat down, each eager to tell the others what the whole elephant was like.
pages.prompt: Four friends sit in a semicircle on a low yard bench while the calm elephant and caretaker remain farther behind.

pages.zh: “是柱子！”“是扇子！”“是绳子！”他们越说越急，谁也说服不了谁。
pages.en: “A pillar!” “A fan!” “A rope!” They grew more impatient, but no one could convince the others.
pages.prompt: Four friends discuss their different conclusions with puzzled expressive gestures, no ridicule or aggression; elephant behind them.

pages.zh: 照料员问：“你们摸到的，是大象同一个地方吗？”大家慢慢安静下来。
pages.en: The caretaker asked, “Did you all touch the same part of the elephant?” Slowly, everyone grew quiet.
pages.prompt: Caretaker kneels or sits at the friends' level and asks a thoughtful question; they pause attentively.

pages.zh: 这回，阿青也摸摸耳朵，阿黄也摸摸腿。果然，每个地方都不一样。
pages.en: This time, A-Qing felt the ear, and A-Huang felt a leg. Each part was different indeed.
pages.prompt: Caretaker supports a new turn: A-Qing in green gently touches the broad ear while A-Huang in ochre touches the outside of a leg; no crowd beneath elephant.

pages.zh: 他们又轮流了解别的部位，把各自摸到的，仔细讲给朋友听。
pages.en: They took turns exploring more parts and carefully described what they had felt to one another.
pages.prompt: A-Lan and A-Zi talk with the other two friends beside the resting elephant; caretaker indicates its different parts; calm shared learning.

pages.zh: 粗粗的腿、宽宽的耳朵、长长的鼻子，还有细尾巴，原来都在同一头大象身上。
pages.en: Thick legs, broad ears, a long trunk, and a thin tail—all belonged to the same elephant.
pages.prompt: Wide clear view of the single elephant with all four body parts naturally visible; four friends and caretaker stand together at a comfortable side distance.

pages.zh: 阿青说：“我只摸到腿，就以为那是全部。原来，我还知道得太少。”
pages.en: A-Qing said, “I felt only the leg and thought it was the whole. I still had so much to learn.”
pages.prompt: A-Qing in green reflects kindly with the three friends on the bench; no shame or mocking faces.

pages.zh: 只知道一部分，就急着判断全部，这就是盲人摸象。多听、多问，才能了解更多。
pages.en: Knowing only one part and rushing to judge the whole is called mistaking a part for the whole. Listening and asking help us learn more.
pages.prompt: All four friends listen to the caretaker's further explanation beside the elephant; open thoughtful body language, no teaching text.

pages.zh: 大象轻轻甩了甩鼻子。朋友们笑着再问一个问题，这一次，谁也不急着下结论。
pages.en: The elephant gently swayed its trunk. The friends smiled and asked another question. This time, no one rushed to a conclusion.
pages.prompt: Warm final yard scene: calm elephant sways its trunk, four friends and caretaker continue a friendly curious conversation; natural unchanged faces.
